title: Unramified coefficient DVR extension and compatible complete local lifting
statement: Let $W$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with uniformizer $\pi$ and perfect residue field $k_0=W/\pi W$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $k'/k_0$ be any field extension. Then there are a complete discrete valuation ring $V$, an injective local map $W\to V$, and an isomorphism $V/\pi V\cong k'$ inducing the specified map on $k_0$. In particular $\pi$ is a uniformizer of $V$. The map $W\to V$ is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topologies [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Moreover, let $(C,\mathfrak n)$ be a complete Noetherian local $W$-algebra with local structure map, and let $s:k'\to C/\pi C$ be a $k_0$-algebra map inducing an isomorphism $k'\cong C/\mathfrak n$. Then the composite $V\to k'\xrightarrow{s}C/\pi C$ lifts to a local $W$-algebra homomorphism $V\to C$.

source.place: Expose IV 4.2.5, first paragraph (formally smooth coefficient extension W_0′→V), second paragraph (lifting V→A′); supporting stated results IV 4.1.3–4.1.6.

proof.text: First show that $k'/k_0$ is formally smooth with the discrete topology. Given a $k_0$-algebra $D$, a square-zero ideal $J$, and a $k_0$-algebra map $g:k'\to D/J$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-nilpotent-lifting] with $K=k'$ and $N=2$ to obtain a ring lift $f:k'\to D$; $p\cdot1_D=0$ because $D$ is a $k_0$-algebra. Write $i:k_0\to k'$ and $a:k_0\to D$ for the structure maps. For $x\in k_0$, choose $y\in k_0$ with $y^p=x$, using perfectness. Then $f(i(y))-a(y)\in J$, and the characteristic-$p$ binomial identity gives $f(i(x))-a(x)=(f(i(y))-a(y))^p=0$, since $p\ge2$ and $J^2=0$. Thus $f$ is $k_0$-linear. This verifies the lifting condition of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for the zero ideal of the field $k'$, with no finite-generation assumption.

source.place: Tag 0320, lemma-formally-smooth-extensions-easy (3); explicit perfect-base linearity verification for the field lifting theorem; ILO IV 4.1.4 and 4.2.5

proof.text: Every ideal of $W$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so $W$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The field $E=k'$ is a Noetherian local ring with zero maximal ideal, and it is complete for that ideal: every quotient $E/0^n$ is $E$ with identity transition maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-from-residue-field] to $A_0=W$, its specified residue field $k_0$, and $E=k'$ with the formal smoothness just proved. Obtain a complete Noetherian local ring $(V,\mathfrak m_V)$, a local map $h:W\to V$ formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_V$-adic topology, and a $W$-algebra isomorphism $e:V/\pi V\xrightarrow{\sim}k'$. The $W$-linearity of $e$ says exactly that the induced map on $k_0$ is the specified inclusion. Here and below $\pi$ in $V$ denotes $h(\pi)$.

source.place: Tag 07NR, lemma-lift-fs, statement; ILO IV 4.1.6 and 4.2.5, first paragraph

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-local-flat], $h$ is flat; both rings are Noetherian and $h$ is local, as required. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], tensoring the injective map $W\xrightarrow{\pi}W$ with $V$ remains injective. Under $W\otimes_W V\cong V$, $w\otimes v\mapsto h(w)v$ (inverse $v\mapsto1\otimes v$), it is multiplication by $\pi$. Thus $\pi$ is a nonzerodivisor in $V$. As $V/\pi V\cong k'$ is a nonzero field, $\pi V=\mathfrak m_V$ and $V\ne0$, so all powers of $\pi$ are nonzero. For any nonzero $w\in W$, [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] writes $w=u\pi^n$ with $u$ a unit. Hence $h(w)=h(u)\pi^n\ne0$, proving injectivity of $h$.

source.place: Tag 07NP, lemma-formally-smooth-flat; Algebra Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, final assertion; ILO IV 4.2.5, first paragraph

proof.text: We verify the DVR assertion directly. Completeness implies $\bigcap_n\mathfrak m_V^n=0$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. For $0\ne v\in V$, choose the largest $n$ with $v\in\pi^nV$: such an $n$ exists because the powers are nested and their intersection is zero. Write $v=\pi^nu$; maximality gives $u\notin\pi V=\mathfrak m_V$, so $u$ is a unit. Products of nonzero elements are therefore nonzero, since $\pi$ is a nonzerodivisor. For any nonzero ideal $H$, choose a nonzero element whose exponent $n$ is least among the exponents occurring in $H$. Its unit factor shows $\pi^n\in H$, and every other element is divisible by $\pi^n$; thus $H=\pi^nV$. The zero ideal is principal too. The ring $V$ is consequently a local principal ideal domain with nonzero maximal ideal $(\pi)$, namely a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$ by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. It is complete by construction.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, elementary uniformizer-division argument; ILO IV 4.2.5 assertion that V is a DVR

proof.text: Now let $C$, $\mathfrak n$ and $s$ be as in the statement, and put $J=\pi C$. Locality of $W\to C$ gives $J\subseteq\mathfrak n$, so $J$ is proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient], $C/J$ is complete for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n/J$. Its separatedness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] gives $\bigcap_{m\ge1}(J+\mathfrak n^m)/J=0$, equivalently $J=\bigcap_{m\ge1}(J+\mathfrak n^m)$. Thus $J$ is closed for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology. Also $J^1\subseteq\mathfrak n$, verifying the remaining ideal hypothesis needed for complete-target lifting. This applies even when $\pi$ is a zerodivisor or zero in $C$.

source.place: Tag 0325, lemma-quotient-complete-local; closure condition for More on Algebra Tag 07NJ, lemma-lift-continuous

proof.text: Set $g=s\circ e\circ(V\to V/\pi V):V\to C/J$. This is a $W$-algebra map: $e$ respects the specified residue map, and $s$ is $k_0$-linear. Since $\mathfrak m_V=\pi V$, $g(\mathfrak m_V)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with $R=W$, $S=V$, source ideal $\mathfrak m_V$, target $A=C$, ideal of definition $I=\mathfrak n$, quotient ideal $J=\pi C$, and $r=t=1$. Formal smoothness is from step 2; completeness and the closed-ideal hypotheses are those of step 5. It yields a $W$-algebra map $f:V\to C$ reducing to $g$, with $f(\mathfrak m_V)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. This map is local: elements outside $\mathfrak m_V$ are units and remain units, whereas elements of $\mathfrak m_V$ map into $\mathfrak n$. Its residue map is the given isomorphism induced by $s$. Thus it is the required lift.

source.place: Tag 07NJ, lemma-lift-continuous; ILO IV 4.1.3 and 4.2.5, second paragraph
